_artifact: P032 panel checker commitment record — B0d pre-registration stage.

_c2f_semantics.definition: N is the number of scorer runs per item per panel seat.
fixed_across: all items in the deterministic blind sample
all three scorer configurations (A1, A2, A3)
_c2f_semantics.pre_registration_statement: This value is committed at C2 pre-registration and is published here before B0d publishes. Any change to N after B0d requires re-publishing the protocol as a new B0-revision. It may not be changed by a runner, a harness argument, or a re-run.
_c2f_semantics.naming_note: The protocol prose (§7 C2(f)) names this quantity `N`. The C4 checker (scripts/b3/tier3_checker.py, load_checker_input) reads the top-level key `committed_n` and no other key. `committed_n` is therefore the single machine-authoritative spelling and is deliberately NOT duplicated under a second key `N`, so the file cannot carry two values that disagree.

_consumed_by.semantics: For each panel seat, check (vi.a) counts the RFC-3161 tokens present on disk at panel/checker-inputs/<seat>/run-<i>/notarization_token.tsr and requires that count to equal committed_n exactly. Missing tokens, surplus tokens, or a count mismatch is a protocol violation and invalidates that scorer's run per C3.
_consumed_by.why_it_matters: RFC-3161 notarization proves that the shown runs happened. It cannot on its own prove that no other runs happened. The committed N is what turns a set of notarized runs into a set that can be checked for arithmetic completeness. Without an N committed before publish, check (vi.a) has nothing to verify against and a runner could prune the published set silently.
_consumed_by.known_residual_gap: Per §7 C2(g) surface 2.6, check (vi.a) bounds PUBLISHED runs, not EXECUTED runs. A runner who executes N+K calls, notarizes all N+K, and publishes only the best N still passes (vi.a). Committing N closes the prune-after-publish gap, not the surplus-execution gap.

_publication.note: The published results repository does not exist yet; its creation is staged separately (W3.4) and is not performed by this ticket. This file is the in-repo staging copy. scripts/b3/tier3_checker.py takes the panel directory as a runtime --panel-dir argument and hardcodes no absolute panel path, so the staging location is free; it was chosen to sit beside the other B0-committed artifacts the b3 tooling already resolves under ops/projects/P032/B0/ (the pinned TSA trust anchors at ops/projects/P032/B0/tsa/*.pem, referenced by PINNED_TSA_PEM in tier3_checker.py).

_completeness.statement: At B0d this file carries the pre-registered commitment (committed_n) and nothing else. The keys that scripts/b3/tier3_checker.py additionally requires — `adjudicators`, `sample`, `blinded_field_values` — are B3 run outputs (per-scorer prompt hashes, actual prompt bytes, per-run response-metadata hashes, notarization token relpaths) and do not exist at B0d. Running the checker against this file today therefore exits 1 (malformed input) by design. That is the correct and honest state: no placeholder hashes are written here.
_completeness.b3_handoff_requirement: scripts/b3/panel_run_harness.py::publish_panel_checker_artifacts writes panel/checker.json wholesale from its own inputs and does not read a pre-existing file. Its committed_n comes from the module constant COMMITTED_N (= 3) or a caller keyword argument. The B3 assembly step MUST verify that the committed_n it emits equals the 3 committed in this file. That equality is currently a convention, not an enforced invariant; see the divergence finding in the accompanying result document.
